title: Sixth Word Applying The Comparison Selling The Trust

questions.question: In the parable’s explanation, who does the king stand for?
questions.answer: He stands for Allah, the Lord and Creator who existed before everything and remains after everything.

questions.question: In this explanation, what do the estate and equipment represent in a person’s life?
questions.answer: They represent the human being’s possessions and abilities in this life, including the body, soul, heart, and inner and outer faculties.

questions.question: Which two examples of human faculties are named as part of this trust?
questions.answer: Examples include the eye and tongue, and also the mind and imagination.

questions.question: Who is represented by the noble lieutenant?
questions.answer: He represents the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.

questions.question: What does the decree in the parable refer to?
questions.answer: It refers to the Qur’an, which explains this spiritual trade.

questions.question: What is the battlefield in the comparison?
questions.answer: It is this world, which is always changing and never stays the same.

questions.question: What question does the changing world push a person to ask?
questions.answer: It makes a person wonder whether what slips away can be turned into something lasting.

questions.question: According to the passage, what answer does the Qur’an give to that question?
questions.answer: It says there is a good and easy way that brings five benefits.

questions.question: What is that way?
questions.answer: It is to return the trust to its real Owner by offering oneself and one’s property to Allah.

questions.question: If someone refuses this trade, what general result follows besides missing its benefits?
questions.answer: That person also suffers five different losses.

questions.question: What is the main message of the passage about a person’s life and abilities?
questions.answer: A person should dedicate his life and faculties to Allah, because they are a trust and doing so brings lasting gain.

questions.question: Why is the parable called a way to see the truth?
questions.answer: Because it helps a person understand spiritual realities through a familiar example.

questions.question: In the explanation of the parable, what belongs to the human trust besides wealth?
questions.answer: It includes one’s body, soul, heart, senses, mind, and imagination.

questions.question: Why is the world compared to a battlefield?
questions.answer: Because it is unstable, full of change, and nothing in it remains in a fixed state.

questions.question: What human concern grows out of seeing the world change so quickly?
questions.answer: People worry that what they hold will disappear and wonder how it can be preserved.

questions.question: Why is this act described as a sale even though everything already belongs to Allah?
questions.answer: Because the person willingly offers back what was entrusted to him and receives great reward in return.

questions.question: What is the first of the five gains in simple terms?
questions.answer: A short earthly life is turned into a source of eternal benefit.

questions.question: What is the second gain?
questions.answer: Paradise is granted as the price.

questions.question: What better role can the eye have when it is used properly?
questions.answer: It can help a person read the signs of Allah in creation.

questions.question: How can the tongue rise in value?
questions.answer: By being used with gratitude and awareness of Allah’s provision rather than mere appetite.

questions.question: How does trust in Allah help a person deal with weakness and many needs?
questions.answer: It brings inner peace and keeps the conscience from being crushed by worry and regret.

questions.question: When will those rewards appear in full?
questions.answer: They will appear at the time when a person needs them most.

questions.question: What three figures in the parable are directly explained at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: The king, the lieutenant, and the decree are explained.

questions.question: What is the relationship between the king and the human being in the explanation?
questions.answer: The king is the One who owns, creates, and sustains the person and all that the person has.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by calling a person’s faculties a trust?
questions.answer: It means they are given by Allah for responsible use, not for selfish misuse.

questions.question: Which parts of the person are included in this trust according to the passage?
questions.answer: The body, spirit, heart, senses, intellect, and imagination are all included.

questions.question: Why is the Qur’an connected with the decree in the parable?
questions.answer: Because it gives Allah’s guidance about this exchange and teaches what it means.

questions.question: What verse’s message is highlighted in the passage?
questions.answer: That Allah takes from believers their selves and wealth in exchange for Paradise.

questions.question: What is the effect of the world’s constant change on human thinking?
questions.answer: It makes people realize their possessions are slipping away and pushes them to seek a lasting answer.

questions.question: What is the “beautiful and easy” solution presented?
questions.answer: To hand the trust back to its true Owner by living for Allah.

questions.question: What does the first profit teach about time spent for Allah?
questions.answer: It teaches that time used for Him is not wasted but becomes everlasting in result.

questions.question: What is the direct exchange named as the second profit?
questions.answer: Paradise is received in return.

questions.question: What final support is given for the fifth profit?
questions.answer: Spiritually perceptive people are said to confirm that worship returns as Paradise’s fruits.

questions.question: What warning closes the passage’s main section?
questions.answer: Refusing this trade does not only cancel the gains; it brings serious losses as well.

questions.question: In the explanation of the parable, what does the king’s ownership teach about human ownership?
questions.answer: It teaches that what people call their own is actually entrusted to them by Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage include under a person’s “property”?
questions.answer: It includes not just wealth, but also the self, inner life, and all human faculties.

questions.question: Why is the Messenger of Allah connected with the noble lieutenant?
questions.answer: Because he delivers Allah’s guidance and calls people to the right response.

questions.question: What role does the Qur’an play in the passage?
questions.answer: It gives the divine instruction that explains the trade between the believer and Allah.

questions.question: Why is the world described as stormy and always shifting?
questions.answer: To show that earthly life is unstable and cannot be held onto forever.

questions.question: What important spiritual question rises from this instability?
questions.answer: A person asks whether there is a way to save what is passing away.

questions.question: What answer is given to that question?
questions.answer: Yes—there is a way to preserve it by offering it back to Allah.

questions.question: How does this answer change the meaning of loss?
questions.answer: What seems like giving up something becomes a way of keeping it in a better and lasting form.

questions.question: What is the first profit of this exchange?
questions.answer: Temporary life becomes a source of eternal reward.

questions.question: What is the second profit of this exchange?
questions.answer: The believer receives Paradise.

questions.question: What general principle is taught through the examples of the mind, eye, and tongue?
questions.answer: Every human faculty rises or falls depending on whether it is used for Allah or for the lower self.

questions.question: What is the fourth profit connected to human weakness?
questions.answer: Trusting Allah saves a person from crushing inner stress and despair.

questions.question: What is the fifth profit, according to people of spiritual insight?
questions.answer: Worship performed through one’s faculties will return as reward in Paradise.

questions.question: What transition does the passage make after listing the five profits?
questions.answer: It warns that turning away from this exchange leads to five losses.

questions.question: Who is being addressed at the beginning of the target passage?
questions.answer: The human self that is pulled by desires and whims is being addressed.

questions.question: Why does the passage use a parable before explaining the truth directly?
questions.answer: It uses the story to make a deep spiritual lesson easier to understand.

questions.question: According to the explanation, what reality does the king symbolize?
questions.answer: He symbolizes Allah as the absolute ruler and owner of all things.

questions.question: What does the explanation teach about a person’s body and abilities?
questions.answer: They are trusts from Allah, not independent possessions.

questions.question: Which guide in the parable points people toward the right choice?
questions.answer: The noble lieutenant, representing the Messenger of Allah, guides them.

questions.question: What divine source explains the trade mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: The Qur’an explains it.

questions.question: What condition of the world is stressed in the image of battle?
questions.answer: The world is unstable and always changing.

questions.question: What natural human concern comes from seeing this instability?
questions.answer: People fear losing what they have and want to know if it can be preserved.

questions.question: What solution is presented as both beautiful and easy?
questions.answer: To give the trust back to its true Owner, Allah.

questions.question: Why does this “sale” lead to gain rather than loss?
questions.answer: Because Allah gives back far more than what the person appears to give up.

questions.question: What is the first gain listed?
questions.answer: A fading life becomes everlasting in outcome.

questions.question: What is the second gain listed?
questions.answer: Paradise is granted as the return.

questions.question: How does the passage show that the use of a faculty changes its value?
questions.answer: It gives examples showing each faculty becomes noble when used for Allah and corrupt when used for the self.

questions.question: What is the elevated use of the tongue?
questions.answer: It is to appreciate Allah’s provision with gratitude.

questions.question: How does faith affect the way a person handles these trusts?
questions.answer: Faith leads a person to use them according to Allah’s purpose and boundaries.

questions.question: What comfort comes from the fourth profit?
questions.answer: A person who relies on Allah is protected from being crushed inwardly by weakness and hardship.

questions.question: What assurance is given in the fifth profit?
questions.answer: Acts of worship done through one’s faculties will return as reward in the next life.

questions.question: What warning is given at the end of the target passage?
questions.answer: Refusing this exchange means not only missing the profits but also facing five losses.

questions.question: What truth is the reader told to see through the parable?
questions.answer: The reader is told to understand the real meaning of human life, possessions, and responsibility before Allah.

questions.question: In the passage, how is Allah described through the symbol of the king?
questions.answer: He is described as the eternal ruler, the Lord, and the Creator.

questions.question: What human qualities and possessions are counted as part of the trust?
questions.answer: A person’s body, soul, heart, senses, reason, imagination, and other abilities are all part of it.

questions.question: What is the significance of linking the lieutenant to the Prophet, peace be upon him?
questions.answer: It shows that prophetic guidance leads people to the right response to Allah’s command.

questions.question: Why is the Qur’an central to the explanation?
questions.answer: Because it clearly teaches the spiritual exchange being discussed.

questions.question: What does the image of a battlefield teach about worldly life?
questions.answer: It teaches that worldly life is unstable, uncertain, and always passing away.

questions.question: What thought does this passing nature of the world awaken in people?
questions.answer: It awakens the desire to save what would otherwise be lost.

questions.question: What is the passage’s answer to the problem of loss?
questions.answer: The answer is to return what was entrusted to Allah, its true Owner.

questions.question: How many major benefits does this path include?
questions.answer: It includes five major benefits.

questions.question: What is the first benefit?
questions.answer: What is temporary gains eternal value when used for Allah.

questions.question: What is the second benefit?
questions.answer: The believer receives Paradise.

questions.question: Why is the intellect a strong example in this discussion?
questions.answer: Because it can either become a source of misery or a means of spiritual understanding, depending on how it is used.

questions.question: What does the eye become if it follows selfish desire?
questions.answer: It becomes a low servant of lust and attachment to temporary things.

questions.question: What does the eye become if it is used for Allah?
questions.answer: It becomes a means of seeing the signs and beauty of Allah’s creation in the right way.

questions.question: What lesson is taught by the example of the tongue and taste?
questions.answer: Even basic physical faculties can become noble through gratitude or degraded through selfishness.

questions.question: On what basis does the believer gain a Paradise-worthy nature?
questions.answer: By using Allah’s trust for Allah’s sake and within His limits.

questions.question: What is the fourth profit for a person living with many needs and weaknesses?
questions.answer: Trust in Allah brings peace and keeps a person from being overwhelmed by distress.

questions.question: What is the fifth profit according to spiritually insightful people?
questions.answer: The worship done through one’s faculties will be returned as reward in Paradise.

questions.question: What final choice is placed before the reader in the target passage?
questions.answer: The reader must choose either the fivefold profit of offering the trust to Allah or the losses that come from refusing it.
